thread:
dmitri: FYI ran night perf job and saw a spike in OOMs on rtx-pool after the kernel-selection change (fused-attn v2 promoted by auto-select).
liz: ugh, saw alerts too. any quick repro or noisy model?
mariam: looks correlated with sequences > 1024 + long-context chat workloads. profiler shows workspace alloc ballooning.
dmitri: exact trace: allocate_workspace(1200MB) failed when running fused_attn_v2 for seq_len 1536. fallback to fused-attn-v1 avoids the big workspace. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:13:12Z] worker-23 ERROR oom allocating 1258291200 bytes for fused_attn_v2 workspace
[2026-03-15T02:13:12Z] worker-23 INFO falling back to fused_attn_v1
[2026-03-15T02:13:12Z] scheduler WARN KV prefill reserved 1.1GiB, fragmentation -> high
```
jon: that suggests kernel-selection heuristic ignored per-request kv cap. We recently bumped default per_request_kv_cap to 1024 tokens in commit 5f2a3c.
sam: timeline: commit 5f2a3c (kv cap 1024) + kernel-select auto-promote fused-attn-v2 (commit bea9) landed in same rollout window.
liz: quick question — are we seeing increased fragmentation or just large contiguous allocations? profiler heap map shows many small free ranges between pinned KV slabs -> fragmentation.
mariam: confirmed. KV prefill now reserves bigger slabs per request, but allocator slab granularity stayed 64MB; many half-used slabs cause unusable free fragments.
dmitri: repro script (local):
```
# reproduce high workspace demand
run_infer --model redwood-open-70B --seq 1536 --prefill_tokens 1536 --kv_cap 1024
```
sam: mitigation options:
- lower per_request_kv_cap back to 384/512
- adjust slab_size_mb to 32 and enable compact-slab pass
- change kernel-select to prefer v1 when seq_len > 1024 or memory pressure high
liz: I'd prefer a short-term config flip + rollout: set per_request_kv_cap=512 and enable compact-slab=true. gives fast rollback.
jon: plus a minor allocator tweak: coalesce adjacent free fragments on free() if combined >= slab_size_mb.
mariam: I'm worried about perf regression if we force fused-attn-v1 on all long sequences. Can we update kernel heuristic to consult current free bytes and fragmentation score?
dmitri: agree. proposed immediate action:
1) rollback default per_request_kv_cap -> 512 in prod config and add override for heavy workloads. (owner: liz)
2) hotfix allocator: enable compact-slab pass at free() to coalesce quickly. (owner: mariam)
3) kernel-select: add memory-aware predicate (free_contiguous >= kernel_workspace_need) and fallback to v1 when false. (owner: sam)
4) add perf test in CI that runs seq 1536 chat workload under two kernels to catch OOM/regressions. (owner: jon)

liz: I'll push config change to infra-configs and roll a canary in us-west-2 now. patch roughly:
```
kv:
  per_request_kv_cap: 512
  global_reserve_mb: 1024
allocator:
  slab_size_mb: 32
  compact_slab: true
kernel_select:
  mem_aware: true
```

ci-bot: running regression pipeline: perf/oom/long-context test queued (job id 9982)
infra-bot: canary rollout started: infra-configs v2026.3.15-rc2 -> us-west-2 (5 nodes)

jon: to capture fragmentation metric, add new gauge: kv_fragmentation_ratio = (total_free_bytes - largest_free_range) / total_free_bytes. alert if > 0.6.
mariam: good idea. I'll add that to runtime metrics and a dashboard tile.
dmitri: note for postmortem: root cause seems to be interaction between larger per-request kv reservation + kernel that requires large contiguous workspace. two independent changes combined produced OOMs.
liz: canary is healthy so far, memory pressure down 40% on canary nodes :thumbsup:
sam: will send PR for kernel-select mem check shortly.
dmitri: thanks. after hotfix and metric, we should schedule a perf knob review — maybe make per_request_kv_cap workload-profiled rather than global default.
liz: sounds good. I'll update the tracker.
mariam: I pushed allocator compact-slab branch, tests pass locally. will open PR with bench results.
dmitri: awesome. assign follow-ups in the thread comments and close when PRs merged. :eyes:
